question: We are hiring our first employee in Singapore. Explain how CPF registration and contribution duties differ from MOM salary-payment duties, and what facts you need from us before applying the rules. Please cover both authorities. Do not calculate payroll or create journal entries.
reviewFocus: Covers both authorities, separates duties, asks for material employee/pay facts, and does not fabricate eligibility, rates, amounts or journals.

modelRequests.systemFirstLine: Interpret the user question only. Do not answer it or provide accounting, tax, or legal conclusions. Do not invent rules. Identify governing versus contextual authorities. Return only one JSON object matching the requested schema; no explanation or reasoning.

modelRequests.candidateText: {"claims":[{"id":"c1","kind":"RULE","text":"Under Central Provident Fund Board rules effective from 1 January 2026, employer and employee contributions depend on employee age and wage tiers, such as for private sector employees where ordinary wages are capped at an ordinary wage ceiling of $8,000, and total CPF contributions and employee shares are computed according to specific age-based tables and rounding rules.","supportIds":["passage-1"],"factRefs":["fact-current-question"],"issueId":"issue_d9895b19"},{"id":"c2","kind":"RULE","text":"Under Ministry of Manpower guidance, employers must pay salary at least once a month and within 7 days after the end of the salary period, and non-payment of salary is an offence.","supportIds":["passage-4"],"factRefs":["fact-current-question"],"issueId":"issue_3ed46661"},{"id":"c3","kind":"RULE","text":"Under Ministry of Manpower guidance effective 1 April 2016, all employers must issue itemised pay slips and keep detailed employment records, including salary records, for employees covered by the Employment Act.","supportIds":["passage-21","passage-22"],"factRefs":["fact-current-question"],"issueId":"issue_3ed46661"}]}

Table 1
CPF Contribution Rate Table from 1 January 2026
rd
for Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents (3 year onwards)
Employee’s Employee’s total wages | Total CPF contributions | Employee’s share
Age (Years) for the calendar month | (Employer’s & Employee’s share) | of CPF contributions
$50 or less | Nil | Nil
> $50 to $500 | 17% (TW) | Nil
55 & below > $500 to $750 | 17% (TW) + 0.6 (TW - $500) | 0.6 (TW - $500)
[37% (OW)]* + 37% (AW) | [20% (OW)]* + 20% (AW)
> $750
* Max. of $2,960 | * Max. of $1,600
$50 or less | Nil | Nil
> $50 to $500 | 16% (TW) | Nil
Above 55 - 60 > $500 to $750 | 16% (TW) + 0.54 (TW - $500) | 0.54 (TW - $500)
[34% (OW)]* + 34% (AW) | [18% (OW)]* + 18% (AW)
> $750
* Max. of $2,720 | * Max. of $1,440
$50 or less | Nil | Nil
> $50 to $500 | 12.5% (TW) | Nil
Above 60 - 65 > $500 to $750 | 12.5% (TW) + 0.375 (TW - $500) | 0.375 (TW - $500)
[25% (OW)]* + 25% (AW) | [12.5% (OW)]* + 12.5% (AW)
> $750
*Max. of $2,000 | * Max. of $1,000
$50 or less | Nil | Nil
> $50 to $500 | 9% (TW) | Nil
Above 65 - 70 > $500 to $750 | 9% (TW) + 0.225 (TW - $500) | 0.225 (TW - $500)
[16.5% (OW)]* + 16.5% (AW) | [7.5% (OW)]* + 7.5% (AW)
> $750
* Max. of $1,320 | * Max. of $600
$50 or less | Nil | Nil
> $50 to $500 | 7.5% (TW) | Nil
Above 70 | > $500 to $750 | 7.5% (TW) + 0.15 (TW - $500) | 0.15 (TW - $500)
[12.5% (OW)]* + 12.5% (AW) | [5% (OW)]* + 5% (AW)
> $750
* Max. of $1,000 | * Max. of $400
Notes:
For Private Sector / Non-Pensionable Employees (Ministries, Statutory Bodies & Aided Schools)
OW: Ordinary Wages (capped at OW ceiling of $8,000)
AW: Additional Wages
TW: Total Wages = OW + AW
Max: Maximum contribution on OW
Steps to compute CPF contribution:
1) Compute the total CPF contribution (rounded to the nearest dollar), i.e., to be rounded down for an amount less than 50 cents and rounded up for an amount of 50
cents and above.
2) Compute the employee’s share of CPF contribution (rounded down to the nearest dollar).
3) Employer’s share = Total contribution - Employee’s share
4) If there is only OW payable for the month, the maximum contribution on OW is to be rounded to the nearest dollar for the total CPF contributions and rounded down
to the nearest dollar for employee’s share of CPF contributions. If there are OW and AW payable for the same month, compute and sum up the CPF contributions
that are payable for OW and AW and apply the rounding rules accordingly.
5) To compute CPF contributions, use the CPF contribution calculator (cpf.gov.sg/employer > Tools and services > Calculators > CPF contribution calculator).
These rates are also applicable to 1st and 2nd year Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) employees and their employers after CPF Board approves their joint application
to contribute to CPF at full employer- full employee rates.

You are using a version of browser which will not be supported after 27 May 2018. To continue to transact with MOM securely, please follow these steps to enable the Transport Layer Security (TLS) of your web browser, or upgrade to the latest version of your browser.

PH pay, COMPASS, Primary Care Plan, myMOM Portal, paying salary, annual leave

•

•

•

•

•

•

•

In accordance with the Employment Act, your employer must pay your salary at least once a month and within 7 days after the end of the salary period. There are exceptions for overtime, resignation without notice and other situations.

If you are facing a salary dispute, you should get advice from the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM). Use the "Ask TADM" chatbot for immediate answers or make an appointment to speak with a TADM advisory officer. You can also file your claims through the TADM eServices, or approach your union if you are a union member.

Salary refers to remuneration, including allowances, paid for work done under a contract of service.

It does not include:

• The value of accommodation, utilities or other amenities.

• Pension or provident fund contribution paid by the employer.

• Travelling allowance.

• Payments for expenses incurred during work.

• Gratuity payable on discharge or retirement.

• Retrenchment benefits.

Singapore does not have a minimum wage. Your salary is subject to negotiation and agreement between your employer and you or your trade union.

If you are covered by the Employment Act, your employer must pay your salary at least once a month.

They can also pay it at shorter intervals if they choose.

Salary must be paid:

• Within 7 days after the end of the salary period

• For overtime work, within 14 days after the end of the salary period

Your final salary payment could vary depending on the following situations:

 In this situation  |  Your final salary must be paid

 Employee resigns and serves the required notice period  |  On the last day of employment.

 Employee resigns and does not serve the notice period  |  Within 7 days of the last day of employment.

 Dismissal on grounds of misconduct  

On the last day of employment.

If this is not possible, then within 3 working days from date of dismissal.

 Employer terminates the contract  

On the last day of employment.

If this is not possible, then within 3 working days from date of termination.

• If your contract involves commission, how and when the commission is paid depends on what is in your employment contract or existing policies or practices.

• If you’re a foreign employee who is leaving your employment, your employer is required to withhold all your monies due to you for tax clearance for up to 30 days upon giving notice of the cessation of your employment to the Comptroller of Income Tax. The monies include your salary, leave pay, etc.

Salary should be paid:

• On a working day, during working hours.

• At your place of work, or any other place you and your employer have agreed on.

Payment can be made:

• Directly into your bank account.

• By cheque. The cheque needs to be cleared by your bank before you’re considered paid.

From 1 April 2016, all employers must issue itemised pay slips to employees covered by the Employment Act.

From 1 April 2016, employers must keep detailed employment records, including salary records, of employees covered by the Employment Act.

Non-payment of salary is an offence.

Your employer must pay your salary on time.

If you are not paid on time, approach your employer to understand if there are reasons for the late payment, and whether the regular payment schedule can be resumed.

If you do not receive your salary, you can file an employment-related claim at the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM), or approach your union for assistance.

File your claim early – don’t wait for the amount to accumulate. There are limits to the claim amount and timeline for filing.

finalResponse.messageText:
# Answer

Under Ministry of Manpower guidance, employers must pay salary at least once a month and within 7 days after the end of the salary period, and non-payment of salary is an offence. [MOM: Paying salary](https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/paying-salary)

Under Ministry of Manpower guidance effective 1 April 2016, all employers must issue itemised pay slips and keep detailed employment records, including salary records, for employees covered by the Employment Act. [MOM: Paying salary](https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/paying-salary)

### Conditions and unresolved points

Some claims could not be established from the admitted evidence and stated facts, so they have been withheld.

- The available admitted evidence does not establish a supported explanation of CPF registration and contribution duties.

- The available admitted evidence does not establish a supported explanation of difference between CPF and MOM duties.

- The available admitted evidence does not establish a supported explanation of facts needed before applying rules.

- The available admitted evidence does not establish whether CPF Treatment of Ordinary Wages applies to your circumstances.

AW: Additional Wages
TW: Total Wages = OW + AW
Max: Maximum contribution on OW
Steps to compute CPF contribution:
1) Compute the total CPF contribution (rounded to the nearest dollar), i.e., to be rounded down for an amount less than 50 cents and rounded up for an amount of 50
cents and above.
2) Compute the employee’s share of CPF contribution (rounded down to the nearest dollar).
3) Employer’s share = Total contribution - Employee’s share
4) If there is only OW payable for the month, the maximum contribution on OW is to be rounded to the nearest dollar for the total CPF contributions and rounded down
to the nearest dollar for employee’s share of CPF contributions. If there are OW and AW payable for the same month, compute and sum up the CPF contributions
that are payable for OW and AW and apply the rounding rules accordingly.
5) To compute CPF contributions, use the CPF contribution calculator (cpf.gov.sg/employer > Tools and services > Calculators > CPF contribution calculator).
These rates are also applicable to 1st and 2nd year Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) employees and their employers after CPF Board approves their joint application
to contribute to CPF at full employer- full employee rates.
